clue.text: Would-be barber on the rampage — all hide!

indicators.note: something on the rampage runs wild, so the letters of the two words that follow are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A crazed would-be hairdresser is running amok, and everyone is told to take cover.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Would-be barber' is a wry description: Delilah had Samson's hair cut off to rob him of his strength.
explanation.definitionFit: In the Bible Delilah arranged for Samson's locks to be shorn, making her a barber of sorts.

clue.text: Absolutely empty lavatory is lethal

parts.note: dead means absolutely, as in dead certain

indicators.note: an emptied word loses its insides, leaving only the outer letters of lavatory

explanation.surface: A completely deserted toilet is somehow a deadly place.
explanation.definitionFit: Deadly and lethal are synonyms: both describe something able to kill.

clue.text: Bully the French soon

parts.note: le is the French for the (masculine)
anon is an old word for soon

explanation.surface: An instruction to intimidate the French before long.
explanation.definitionFit: To lean on someone is an idiom for pressuring or intimidating them, as a bully does.

clue.text: Left most of Essex with liver upset — worse things can happen

indicators.note: most of a word means it loses its final letter, here the last of Essex
upset means the letters of liver are knocked into a different order

explanation.surface: Someone has left Essex (an English county) with a liver complaint, but consoles themself that it could be worse.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a whole phrase: settling for the lesser evil is what you do when worse things could happen.
explanation.definitionFit: Choosing the lesser evil means accepting a bad option because the alternative would be worse.

clue.text: Should the East stop ignoring borders?

indicators.note: each of the three words drops its outside letters, its borders, keeping only what lies within

explanation.surface: A political question: ought the East to stop disregarding frontiers?
explanation.definitionFit: Has to expresses obligation, the same sense as should in 'you should go'.

clue.text: Things found in yachts regularly after back-to-back parties

indicators.note: after says the picked letters come later than the parties

parts.note: a party is a do

indicators.note: back to back means a second party faces the other way, so it is read in reverse beside the first
taking letters regularly means every other letter of yachts

explanation.surface: Odd items turn up in yachts once a run of parties is over.
explanation.definitionFit: Doodahs is informal for unnamed objects, much like thingummies or whatsits.

clue.text: Stressed at first, man hoovered shoddily

indicators.note: done shoddily, the letters are put together badly, in a jumbled order
at first takes only the opening letter of man

explanation.surface: A man's first attempt at vacuuming was slapdash.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive home a point is an idiom for emphasising or stressing it.

clue.text: See 26
Still taking no sides, refer to uprising

indicators.note: with no sides, taking loses its outer letters at each end
in a down entry, uprising means the word climbs, read from bottom to top

parts.note: to cite is to refer to

explanation.surface: A neutral observer, staying out of it, mentions a revolt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uprising' turns CITE into ETIC beneath AKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Akinetic is a medical term for lacking movement, so it means motionless.

clue.text: Running cadence of horse mostly circling donkey

indicators.note: circling says the shortened horse goes round the donkey
mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a steed is a horse
a donkey is a fool, and so is a prat

explanation.surface: A horse's running rhythm, almost encircling a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'donkey' here is the insult for a fool rather than the animal.
explanation.definitionFit: A runner's step rate is the number of strides per minute, their cadence.

clue.text: First service at 10

parts.note: A is first in the alphabet and a grade for first
Mass is a church service

explanation.surface: The first church service takes place at ten o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not a time: it points to 10 across, STOCKPILE.
explanation.definitionFit: To amass is to gather up a large store, which is to stockpile.

clue.text: Fancy pickles to stash

indicators.note: fancy describes something elaborate or made up, signalling that the letters of pickles to are rearranged

explanation.surface: Elaborate pickles are put away for later.
explanation.definitionFit: A stockpile is a hoard kept in reserve, much as a stash is.

clue.text: Missed having part exchange reviewed

indicators.note: the two parts of the word swap places, the front section moving round to the back

parts.note: to have overlooked something is to have missed it

explanation.surface: Someone missed the trade-in offer at the car dealer, and it was reviewed.
explanation.walkthrough: Part exchange is the British term for trading in an old item against a new one; here the parts OVER and LOOKED change places.
explanation.definitionFit: To look something over is to examine or check it, so looked over means reviewed.

clue.text: Long short time

indicators.note: short says the word is cut, losing its final letter

parts.note: to long for something is to yearn

explanation.surface: A paradox: a time that is both long and short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A year is a period of time, twelve months long.

clue.text: No-hopers mislaid baggage containing uniform

parts.note: something mislaid is lost

indicators.note: containing says the baggage holds the uniform letter inside it

parts.note: cases are baggage
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Hopeless travellers have lost their luggage, which held a uniform.
explanation.definitionFit: A lost cause is a venture or person with no chance of success, a no-hoper.

clue.text: Hotlines got crossed for student of culture

indicators.note: crossed lines are tangled, so the letters of hotlines got are jumbled together

explanation.surface: Telephone hotlines got their wires crossed, confusing a scholar.
explanation.definitionFit: An ethnologist studies peoples and their cultures, comparing their customs.

clue.text: Trouble with Cats? Musical rubbish

parts.note: Hair is a 1960s rock musical
balls is slang for nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A grumble that the musical Cats was a load of rubbish.
explanation.walkthrough: With 'Musical' beside it, 'Cats' reads as the Lloyd Webber show; it really means the animals.
explanation.definitionFit: Hairballs are a common trouble for cats, which cough them up after grooming.

clue.text: Has an evening meal, including potatoes, and crashes

indicators.note: including says the meal word holds the potatoes inside it

parts.note: sups means has supper, an evening meal
mash is mashed potatoes

explanation.surface: Someone eats dinner with potatoes and then crashes out.
explanation.definitionFit: Smash-ups are violent collisions, especially road crashes.

clue.text: Diagnose problem that expressed mental stress

indicators.note: a problem with the word diagnose leaves its letters in disorder

explanation.surface: A doctor diagnoses a problem that was causing mental distress.
explanation.definitionFit: Agonised describes a look or cry showing great anguish of mind.

clue.text: Wonderful publication: Guardian, finally providing Matilda with little money!

parts.note: a mag, short for magazine, is a publication

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of Guardian

parts.note: if means providing, as in providing it rains
Matilda is the setter, so stands for I
a cent is a small coin, a little money

explanation.surface: The setter boasts of a wonderful newspaper, the Guardian, which at last pays her a little.
explanation.definitionFit: Magnificent and wonderful both mean splendid or impressive.

clue.text: They say you are each in love with this museum

indicators.note: in says the second sounded letter is placed inside love as well, apart from the first
each, read with in, says the first sounded letter also goes inside love on its own

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: they say means these words are spoken, so their sound gives the letters

parts.note: you sounds like the letter U
are sounds like the letter R, as in text-speak

explanation.surface: People tell you that you will each fall for this museum.
explanation.walkthrough: 'each in' means the two sounded letters go into love separately, not as a pair.
explanation.definitionFit: The Louvre in Paris is the world's most visited art museum.

clue.text: Personified sleep getting endless hype? Not so!

indicators.note: endless applies to each of the three words, so each loses its final letter

explanation.surface: Is sleep being overhyped? Someone insists it is not.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' strips E from hype, T from Not and O from so.
explanation.definitionFit: Hypnos is the Greek god who is the personification of sleep.

clue.text: Crimes contributing to everybody's insecurity

indicators.note: contributing to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Wrongdoing adds to the insecurity everyone feels.
explanation.definitionFit: Sins are moral wrongs or offences, loosely crimes.

clue.text: A girly boot design is essential

indicators.note: a new design reshapes the letters of A girly boot into another arrangement

explanation.surface: A fashion verdict: this girlish boot design is a must-have.
explanation.definitionFit: Something obligatory is required or compulsory, and so essential.

clue.text: Hindus take off clothing and start to swim here?

definitions.text: Hindus take off clothing and start to swim here?

indicators.note: taking off its clothing strips the outer letters from Hindus
start to takes the opening letter of swim

explanation.surface: Is this where Hindus undress and begin to bathe?
explanation.definitionFit: The Indus is a great river of the Indian subcontinent, held sacred in Hindu tradition.

clue.text: Computers etc starting to cause headaches and irritation

parts.note: IT, information technology, covers computers and the like

indicators.note: starting to takes the first letter of each of the next two words

explanation.surface: Computers and the like are beginning to cause headaches and annoyance.
explanation.definitionFit: An itch is an irritation of the skin, and figuratively a nagging annoyance.

clue.text: Outstanding underground network in having no leader

indicators.note: in says the network goes inside the leaderless word

parts.note: unled means without anyone leading
a sett is a badger's burrow, an underground network of tunnels

explanation.surface: An exceptional underground railway system operating without a boss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'underground network' suggests the Tube or a resistance movement; it is a badger's SETT.
explanation.definitionFit: An outstanding bill is unsettled: not yet paid.

clue.text: More than half a dozen trees found in Kent

parts.note: seven is one more than six, half a dozen
oaks are trees

explanation.surface: A count of trees growing in Kent.
explanation.walkthrough: Kent is a county in south-east England; Sevenoaks is one of its towns.
explanation.definitionFit: Sevenoaks is a commuter town located in the county of Kent.

clue.text: Be quiet about a theologian and American holy men

indicators.note: about says the call for quiet goes round the next pieces

parts.note: sh is a call to be quiet
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is a theologian's degree
US means American

explanation.surface: Someone hushes a theologian and some American holy men.
explanation.definitionFit: Sadhus are Hindu ascetics or wandering holy men.

clue.text: Stress fractures overwhelming writer's family members

indicators.note: overwhelming says the jumbled letters engulf the writer
fractures says the word stress is broken up and its letters reassembled

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I; the 's reads as is

explanation.surface: Stress fractures are overwhelming a writer's relatives.
explanation.definitionFit: Sisters are female siblings, members of a family.
